events.title: The First Lateran Council
events.shortBlurb: The first general council held in the West met at Rome to confirm the Concordat of Worms and seal the end of the Investiture Controversy…
body: In March 1123 Callistus II presided in person as some three hundred bishops and more than six hundred abbots of the West assembled at the Lateran, the pope's cathedral in Rome. Convoked the previous December, it was the first general council ever held in the West and is reckoned the ninth ecumenical council of the Church.

Its chief work was the solemn confirmation of the Concordat of Worms, agreed the previous September between the pope and the Emperor Henry V, which had ended the long Investiture Controversy. Both originals of the settlement were read before the fathers and ratified, securing the free election of bishops and abbots and reserving spiritual investiture to the Church alone.

The council also promulgated twenty-two disciplinary canons: it voided the ordinations conferred by the antipope Gregory VIII, forbade marriage to clergy in major orders, protected the families and goods of crusaders, and punished those who molested pilgrims on the road to Rome. So deep was the relief at the peace that chroniclers counted the year 1122 as the beginning of a new era.
